exposure: surgical haemostasis with controlled intrauterine tamponade
Group 3: surgical haemostasis with controlled intrauterine tamponade using vaginal and intrauterine Zhukovsky balloon (n=79)
Group 2: combined compression haemostasis with tourniquets and intrauterine balloon tamponade (n=33)
cohort: 532 women with abnormal placental localization and attachment
finding: Compression haemostasis techniques, particularly surgical haemostasis with controlled intrauterine tamponade using the Zhukovsky balloon, were associated with a reduction in hysterectomies and blood loss in women with placenta praevia and PAS disorders.
